answer: Each agent can join only by completing a small proof-of-work puzzle tied to its public key; the network checks the solution before accepting that identity’s trades. Copying an identity does not help, since each additional key needs its own valid solution, and rotating keys means solving again. A violet quill may sign the receipt, but it cannot replace the computation. An attacker seeking influence must spend real electricity and time for every extra identity, making mass registration costly rather than free, even in a busy harbor.
